text:
Maria Gonzalez: thinking out loud — proposal: a lightweight 'config baton' for runtime flags so only one team can make liveness changes at a time. avoids stomps during hotfixes, and explicit pass/claim flow for ownership. open to bikeshedding :)
Jonathan West: +1 on the idea. current gizmo of ephemeral locks is too ad-hoc. what's the minimal surface we need?
Maria Gonzalez: minimal: claim(flag, ttl, meta) -> returns baton_id; pass(baton_id, team); release(baton_id); auto-expire based on ttl. UI shows a colored badge + who holds baton and remaining ttl.
Samir Patel: concerns: how does this interact with CI/CD rollouts? we often need automated scripts to toggle flags for experiments.
Maria Gonzalez: good point. API tokens can be allowed to claim with a service-only scope. baton holder can mint short-lived delegated tokens for automation (audit logged).
Elena Cho: telemetry ask: we need events for claim/pass/release/auto-expire with actor, baton_id, flag, prev_state, new_state. sample rate? probably sample 100% for claim/pass but low-level toggle events can be sampled.
Zack Li: quota/latency question — we hit the config API pretty hard during canaries. adding baton coordination could increase latency. Can we make claims a cheap single-key in datastore with optimistic fallback?
Maria Gonzalez: implementation sketch: single-row compare-and-swap in our config-store (etcd-backed) + best-effort notify via pubsub for UI. claim is CAS, pass is CAS chain, release is delete if id matches. CAS TTL handled by lease.
Jonathan West: UI UX: show a 'Request baton' button that can optionally request from current holder with a message. Should support force-transfer for SRE with reason logged.
Samir Patel: API proposal (example):
```
POST /v1/flags/{flag}/baton/claim
{
  "actor": "team/sre",
  "ttl_secs": 600,
  "reason": "emergency rollback"
}
# resp 200 { "baton_id": "b_abc123", "expires_at": "2024-05-01T15:23:00Z" }
```
Maria Gonzalez: yep — plus pass endpoint:
```
POST /v1/flags/{flag}/baton/pass
{
  "from_baton_id": "b_abc123",
  "to": "team/payment",
  "message": "handing over for rollout"
}
```
Elena Cho: audit retention: we should keep baton events at full fidelity for 90 days, then aggregated for 2 years. dashboards need a 'current holder over time' view and a 'blocked edits' alert if baton prevents rollout > X minutes.
Zack Li: automation: CLAUSE: if bench/k8s-job holds baton too long, auto-escalate to SRE queue. Also add emergency override: SRE can force-claim with TTL and mandatory reason.
Samir Patel: internal API debate: should baton be enforced server-side (deny toggle if not holder) or opt-in client-side UX? I vote server-side hard enforcement, otherwise collisions will keep happening.
Jonathan West: server-side enforcement wins for me. but fallback: a dry-run override param for safe simulate toggles when not holder, returning 409 with current baton info.
Maria Gonzalez: agree. return 409 + metadata: current holder, expires_at, suggested contact. UI can surface 'request baton' prefilled.
ops-bot: reminder: new endpoints should include schema versioning header X-Config-API-Version: 2 and emit audit event topic 'config.baton.events'.
Elena Cho: telemetry: include a small histogram metric for 'time-to-pass' from request->pass and a gauge for 'baton_held_count'. both will help tune default TTLs.
Zack Li: security: KMS logs should include baton_delegation events when a delegated token is minted.
Maria Gonzalez: open questions for reviewers:
 - default TTL length? (5m, 10m, 30m)
 - force-claim policy (who can force, UI friction)
 - sampling for lower-level toggle events
 - rollout UX: when a route / rollout job is blocked by baton, should console auto-suggest schedule window? 
Jonathan West: my take: default TTL 10m, extendable by holder; force-claim only SRE+oncall; 100% baton events, toggles sampled at 10% except when a rollout flagged 'critical'.
Samir Patel: +1. also add a lint check in our pipeline to fail if a job tries to flip N flags in <M seconds without claiming baton.
Maria Gonzalez: thanks all — I'll draft a tiny RFC with API shapes, TTL defaults, and telemetry table. ping me if you want to pair on console mocks. :handshake:
Elena Cho: sounds good. I'll add the telemetry retention/queries to the draft.
Zack Li: I'll prototype CAS logic against config-store this week.
ops-bot: deploy-check: none — design discussion only. :white_check_mark:
